content.text:
This confirms the bug entirely. This same commit added *both* the correct per-type `ApplicationProperty` enum constants (e.g., `ReservationPriorityGroup`, `ReservationPriorityCurriculum`, `ReservationPriorityCourse`) *and* the switch statement that mistakenly used `...Individual` for all of the `Group`, `Curriculum`, and `Course` cases — a clear copy-paste error where the same four lines were duplicated across cases without updating the property name.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 18f154d85110c36f6eb403d0a33703db4cfe8175

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I used `git log --follow -p` on `XReservation.java` to trace the full history of the affected switch statement, searching for when the `Group:`, `Curriculum:`, `Course:` cases and the `ReservationPriorityIndividual` reference first appeared together. This located commit `18f154d8` ("Fri Dec 5 07:23:20 2014"), which is the commit that originally introduced this exact switch statement.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `18f154d8` added the `switch (type)` block in `XReservation`'s constructor, along with a large `ApplicationProperty.java` change that defined distinct configuration properties per reservation type (`ReservationPriorityGroup`, `ReservationPriorityCurriculum`, `ReservationPriorityCourse`, and their `CanOverLimit`/`MustBeUsed`/`AllowOverlap` counterparts). However, in the same commit, the `case Group:`, `case Curriculum:`, and `case Course:` blocks were all written using `ApplicationProperty.Reservation*Individual` instead of their respective type-specific properties — a copy-paste mistake (likely from duplicating the `case Individual:` block without updating the suffix).

**(3) Evidence:** 
- `git show 18f154d8 -- .../XReservation.java` shows the switch statement was newly added in this commit, with all four non-Individual, non-Override, non-Dummy cases (`Group`, `Curriculum`, `Course`) using `...Individual` properties verbatim.
- `git show 18f154d8 -- .../ApplicationProperty.java` shows the correctly-named `Group`/`Curriculum`/`Course` properties were defined in this very same commit, proving they were available and simply not used correctly in `XReservation.java`.
- The bug-fixing commit `6eb8807d` (Feb 2016, over a year later) does nothing but correct these four lines per case to reference the properly-named properties — a direct fix of the original copy-paste error with no other logic changes.

I'm highly confident in this attribution — the fix commit's diff is a mechanical one-to-one correction of the exact lines introduced in `18f154d8`, and no intervening commits touched this switch statement (confirmed via the `--follow -p` history, which showed no other commits modifying these lines between introduction and fix).
